Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates volume loss in the right hemithorax, evidenced by the elevation of the right hemidiaphragm and crowding of vascular structures. A characteristic kinked vessel is visible in the right cardiophrenic angle, which is a specific radiological sign associated with right upper lobe pulmonary hypoplasia (often seen in cases like Scimitar syndrome or isolated hypoplasia).
